These indicators (install-time execution + background detached process + deceptive metadata) justify classifying it as Malware.

There is no justification in the manifest for starting a background process on install, and the dependency list includes many unexpected/unrelated modules (increasing attack surface). The setup.py runs imperative, install-time network and system actions: it git-clones an external repo, downloads remote files, invokes pip to install the cloned code, and deletes directories (including package dirs) all at import/install time. These behaviors enable arbitrary remote code execution, repackaging/typosquatting of an upstream project, and destructive filesystem changes — a high-risk supply-chain pattern consistent with malicious intent. Do not install or run this package.
